title.en: Simple Pendulum and Simple Harmonic Motion

international.topic: Simple pendulum and simple harmonic motion

kcse.topic: Linear motion: determining g with a simple pendulum

summary.en: A swinging bob keeps time: its period depends on the length of the string and on gravity.

text.en: Pull the bob to one side and let go. It swings out, comes back, and repeats. One complete trip there and back is one oscillation. The time it takes is the period T.

Gravity pulls the bob down while the string holds it on a circle. The part of the weight that points back to the centre grows with the displacement. That pull towards the centre is what makes the motion simple harmonic.
Slide the clamp to make the string longer. The swing slows down. For small angles the period depends only on the length L and on g. The mass of the bob does not matter.
The formula works when the swing is small, about 10° or less. A big swing takes slightly longer, so careful experimenters always start with a small angle.
